strings.name: Bob Iger
strings.summary: Bob Iger rose from production work at ABC to lead Disney as CEO from 2005 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2026. He oversaw acquisitions of Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm and Fox assets and advanced direct-to-consumer services including Disney+. Expansion also brought integration, digital-transition and labor-relations challenges. After handing over the CEO role in March 2026, he continued as a senior advisor and director.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 13 November 2026; selected events reach the completed March 2026 CEO handover, with an October interview also corroborating living status. He is a former CEO, senior advisor and director; planned December retirement is not presented as completed.
strings.influence.rationale: Led Disney's acquisitions including Pixar and Marvel, advancing global film, entertainment and streaming businesses.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: BS in television and radio, Ithaca College (1973)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Bringing together global entertainment brands
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Led Disney’s acquisitions of Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm and 21st Century Fox assets, expanding its content and brand portfolio.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Advancing a streaming transition
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Launched Disney+ during his tenure, connecting the group’s content and platforms with direct subscription services.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Hands over Disney’s CEO role
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Handed over to Josh D’Amaro at the annual meeting, ending his second CEO tenure while continuing as senior advisor and director.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Comments on Hollywood strikes
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Called writers’ and actors’ expectations unrealistic and warned of disruption, making his position a focus of the labor dispute.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Returns as Disney CEO
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Returned at the board’s request to replace Bob Chapek and oversee strategy and succession planning.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Steps down as CEO for the first time
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Became executive chair as Chapek took the CEO role, continuing to oversee creative matters until late 2021.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Expands content assets and launches Disney+
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Disney completed its Fox asset acquisition and launched Disney+ in November, accelerating integration of content and subscription platforms.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Acquires Lucasfilm
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Disney brought brands including Star Wars into the group, extending connections among films, merchandise and parks.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Acquires Marvel
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Disney acquired Marvel, expanding its superhero characters and resources for film and television development.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Acquires Pixar
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Disney completed its Pixar acquisition, renewing its long-term relationship with the animation company.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Becomes Disney CEO for the first time
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Moved from president and COO to CEO, beginning a period focused on content brands and technological change.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Joins ABC production
strings.timeline.event-10.text: After local television work, entered ABC production and gradually moved into network management.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Graduates from Ithaca College
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Earned a television-and-radio degree and initially hoped to become a news anchor, working early on as a weatherman.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in New York State
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born and raised in New York State before developing a career in American television and entertainment.
